title: Ann Arbor Heat Pump Rebates 2026: City $4,000 Plus DTE
desc: Ann Arbor heat pump rebates in 2026: the city's A2ZERO rebate pays $4,000 ($5,500 for lower incomes), plus ductwork and water heater help, and DTE rebates for electric homes.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Ann Arbor
lead: An Ann Arbor homeowner or renter can get $4,000 from the city toward a cold climate heat pump, or $5,500 if household income is at or below 120% of area median income. That is much more than the typical utility rebate. Here is what the city pays, what it requires, and how DTE's smaller rebate fits in. We read both on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What heat pump rebates pay in Ann Arbor
cards_intro: The city's page said home energy rebates were open on the day we read it. Rebates cannot be more than 90% of the cost of the measure or project.

cards.title: A2ZERO cold climate heat pump
cards.note: Unit on the NEEP cold climate list, 15.2+ SEER2 and 8+ HSPF2. Dual-fuel systems are not eligible.

cards.title: A2ZERO ductwork
cards.note: Only for changes to existing ducts so the heat pump works well. A post-install static pressure test is required.

cards.title: A2ZERO heat pump water heater
cards.note: UEF of 2.0 or higher, installed by a contractor.

cards.title: A2ZERO electrical panel
cards.note: A main panel of 200 amps or more, or a new sub-panel. Not for new construction.

cards.title: DTE heat pump
cards.note: Only for electric customers replacing electric heating.

cards.title: State rebates (MiHER)
cards.note: Paused for new income-qualified applications in five districts. Ann Arbor's district is not named on the state page.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D tax credits
cards.note: The federal home energy credits ended for work finished after December 31, 2025. A quote that counts on them is out of date.

after_cards:
Do the paperwork in order

The city wants you to reserve funds first, then buy, then finish within 90 days of approval. A heat pump already installed before you reserve is not the path the city describes. Ask the rebate team at 734-726-4747 if you are not sure.
sections: Who gains most in Ann Arbor

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says electricity heats 26.1% of Ann Arbor homes and utility gas heats 70.7%. The electric group saves the most by switching, and can often claim both the city's and DTE's rebates. Gas homes can still claim the city's rebate, since the city's page does not require electric heat, but the savings case is weaker. A heat pump pairs well with an air conditioner that is due for replacement.

The city requires a contractor install, a Manual J sizing report and an AHRI certificate that lists the whole system. Reservation also needs the manufacturer, model number and certificate. Up to two mini-split systems are allowed per address. The rules list the unit as cold climate rated, so ask your installer for the NEEP list entry in writing.

The city's rebate cannot be more than 90% of the cost of the measure or the project. For most heat pump jobs that is not a limit, but a small mini-split job might hit it. Do the math with your quote before you plan around the full $4,000.

Ask each installer how the unit performs on the coldest nights and whether you should keep a backup heat source. The city requires that the unit be on the cold climate list, which helps, but a contractor's sizing report still decides what size you need.
claim_heading: How to claim the Ann Arbor heat pump rebate
claim_steps: Pick a unit from the NEEP cold climate list that meets the city's ratings.
Verify your income with the city if you want the $5,500 amount.
Reserve the rebate funds before you buy and wait for approval.
Have a contractor install it, with a Manual J report and AHRI certificate, within 90 days.
Send in the full application. The check takes 6 to 8 weeks. Apply to DTE separately if you heat with electricity.
faq: How much is the Ann Arbor heat pump rebate?
$4,000, or $5,500 if household income is at or below 120% of area median income.
Does it cover a gas furnace swap?
The city's page does not say the heat pump must replace electric heat. It does say dual-fuel heat pumps are not eligible.
You must finish within 90 days of approval. We did not see an end date for the program, so confirm funds on the city page.
Can I also get DTE's rebate?
Only if you are an electric customer replacing electric heating. DTE pays $150 to $1,200 for that case.
Does the federal credit still exist?
No. The federal heat pump credit ended for work finished after December 31, 2025.
